Posted May 12, 2003
Special Report to MarijuanaNews by Richard Cowan

The refugee hearings for Steve Tuck began today, and will run for most of the rest of the week.

These hearings follow essentially the same format as the hearings for Steve Kubby.
See
 Placer County: Still Crazy After All These Years. Kubby Hearings Offer New Evidence California Law Enforcement Still Fighting Medical Cannabis Law. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

However, there is one major difference. For some reason, the Canadian government thought it necessary to send in some bigger guns, including someone from the Justice Ministry, and a special representative from Immigration, who described himself as a mean S.O.B. I explained that we were from the States, so he could not even begin to qualify as mean by our standards.

As if to try to prove his point, he moved to bar the testimony from witnesses from the Kubby hearings being included as part of Tuck's case.
See
DEAland On Trial At Kubby Refugee Hearings. Damning Testimony From A Patient, A Judge and Ed Rosenthal. Meanwhile, Congress Was Busy Making It Even Worse. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

We objected, of course, and the Adjudicator (judge) overruled his motion. She is really doing everything possible to be fair.

When we got down to substantive matters in the afternoon, the self-described mean S.O.B. quickly realized that this was going to be more complicated than he had anticipated. When Steve explained how he gave seeds to Health Canada for their medical cannabis program, and that Health Canada was referring patients to him to get seeds, it became obvious that this was not going to be a routine case.

Indeed, Tuck's story is one of the most incredible sagas in the bizarre world of cannabis prohibition.
See
 Steve Tuck Smokes Hash with John Walters As Czar Visits Vancouver's New Amsterdam Cafe. Another One We Couldn't Make Up. Of course, Walters Didn't Smoke with Steve, But.. Special to MarijuanaNews

I use the word saga deliberately. His is a heroic narrative in the original sense of the word.
See
 Todd, Steve and Mike; And Why I Do What I Do.

I would greatly prefer to be a simple teller of tales, but now I find myself in a minor supportive role. Because Steve could not afford a real lawyer, I agreed to assist him presenting his case. (That is allowed here, but beware of phony refugee experts, who offer their services for a fee. I am not charging anything, of course.)

In any case, for the next week, I will be more than a little preoccupied, but I will try to bring you daily reports. This is terribly stressful for Steve, as it was for Steve Kubby, so I ask that now more than ever you remember him in your prayers.

As he wrote to the Adjudicator, Can anyone who reads the newspapers and who has followed the exceptional circumstances surrounding these hearings and the behavior of the US and Canadian governments, and even a member of the Canadian Parliament, doubt that I am a political refugee in a highly politicized case?

On the other hand, can anyone imagine that the government of Canada wants to be in the position of saying that sick, dying and disabled Americans cannot get a fair trial?

My hope for living in freedom and dying with dignity rests with you.
